craft_claim: Forward-facing motivational prose persuades when it couples a desired goal (pathways thinking) with articulable agency, rather than asserting a wish or an outcome alone.

supporting_evidence.location: Psychological Inquiry 13(4):249-275, definition and theory sections
supporting_evidence.note: Snyder defines hope as the perceived capability to derive pathways to desired goals and to motivate oneself via agency thinking to use them; high hope is consistently linked to better outcomes across domains.

supporting_evidence.location: Address to the Constituent Assembly, 14-15 August 1947
supporting_evidence.note: Nehru's address repeatedly names a desired future together with the labour required to reach it, refusing ease as the endpoint and pairing vision with route.

counterevidence.note: Goal imagery is not sufficient on its own: possible selves moved academic behaviour only when linked with concrete strategies and congruent identity.

scope: Goal-directed motivational prose across speech, essay, blog, and copy.
exceptions: Purely poetic or devotional uplift (e.g., bhakti-adjacent song) may foreground longing rather than a route and still cohere as tone-lyrical or tone-reverent, not this tone.
